taxonomy:
Here is a taxonomy of the grid-based logic games, using only information from the provided rules:

**I. Cell State Manipulation (Coloring, Shading, Filling)**

*   **A. Coloring/Shading Cells (Black/White):**
    *   **Chained Block:** Fill cells, consecutive black cells form a "block".
    *   **Heyawake:** Fill cells, painted cells cannot be connected horizontally or vertically, white cells must not be separated by painted cells.
    *   **Hitori:** Color cells black so no number appears more than once in a row or column, black cells never touch, white cells form a continuous network.
    *   **Kurodoko:** Color cells black, numbers show white cells to nearest black cell/frame, black cells cannot touch, white cells must be connected.
    *   **Kurotto:** Fill (color) cells, number in circle indicates sum of continuous black cells extending from it.
    *   **LITS:** Color four consecutive squares (tetrominoes) in each area, similarly shaped tetrominoes cannot touch (except corners), colored squares form a connected network, cannot form 2x2 or larger squares.
    *   **Norinori:** Place blocks in twos in consecutive black squares.
    *   **Nurimeizu:** Paint cells to make walls, create a maze from S to G across only white cells.
    *   **Nurimisaki:** Fill cells, cells with circles remain white "Misaki", others cannot be "Misaki", numbers indicate white cells in a straight line from Misaki.
    *   **Nurikabe:** Fill cells, cannot fill cells with numbers, numbers tell continuous white cells, black cells form a continuous wall, black cells cannot be 2x2 or larger.
    *   **Nuritwin:** Shade cells, each region contains two blocks of same number of shaded cells, all shaded cells connected, two blocks in same region must not touch, no 2x2 shaded group.
    *   **Shakashaka:** Place black "triangles in squares", parts of grid remaining white form a rectangle or square, numbers indicate surrounding black triangles.
    *   **Sto-stone:** Fill colored cells, numbers in rooms show continuous black cells, black cells cannot connect across bold lines, dropped stones fill bottom half of grid.
    *   **Tilepaint:** Color tiles, numbers with diagonal lines tell black cells to right/downward, cells of a tile must all be colored or uncolored.
    *   **Usowan:** Fill (colored) cells, cells containing numbers cannot be colored.

*   **B. Placing Symbols/Objects (non-numeric):**
    *   **Akari:** Place light bulbs (circles) in white squares, numbers show adjacent bulbs, bulbs illuminate, every white square illuminated, bulb cannot illuminate another bulb.
    *   **Pencils:** Mark out pencils (straight groups of cells), draw lines from tip, numbers in pencil show length.

**II. Line/Loop Drawing**

*   **A. Single Loop Puzzles:**
    *   **Dotchi-Loop:** Draw lines to make a single loop, through centers of cells, through all white circles, right-angled turn in all white circles in an area, not through black circles.
    *   **Masyu:** Make a single loop with lines, through centers of cells, through all black and white circles, white circles pass straight and turn next to it, black circles turn in cell and go straight next cell.
    *   **Mid-loop:** Draw lines to make a single loop, through centers of cells, through all black circles (midpoint of line segment).
    *   **Moon-or-Sun:** Draw a line to make a single loop, through centers of cells, loop goes through each room once, through all moon cells or all sun cells in a room, alternates moon/sun rooms.
    *   **Nagareru:** Draw a line to make a single continuous loop in a direction, through cells with arrows, arrows show wind direction.
    *   **Slitherlink:** Connect adjacent dots with vertical or horizontal lines to make a single loop, numbers indicate lines surrounding cell.
    *   **Suraromu:** Make a single loop with lines, pass all "Gates" once, starts and returns to open numbered circle, number shows gates to go through.
    *   **Yajilin:** Draw a line to make a single loop, numbers show black cells in direction of arrow, loop not through black cells or numbers, black cells cannot touch.

*   **B. Connecting Paths/Bridges:**
    *   **Hashiwokakero:** Connect islands (circles with numbers) with bridges, number indicates bridges, max two bridges between islands, bridges cannot cross, continuous link.
    *   **Numberlink:** Connect pairs of the same numbers with a continuous line, lines through centers of cells, lines cannot cross/branch/go through numbers.

**III. Grid Division/Regioning**

*   **A. Dividing into Blocks/Regions:**
    *   **Double Choco:** Divide grid into blocks, each block contains a pair of white and gray areas of same form, numbers indicate cells of that color.
    *   **Evolomino:** Paint some cells black, black cells linked vertically and horizontally must form a rectangle or square, white cells must not form a rectangle or square, numbers indicate cells of area.
    *   **Five Cells:** Divide grid into blocks of five cells, numbers show lines of a block around it.
    *   **Fillomino:** Divide board into blocks, fill each block with same number, block contains as many cells as number, same sized blocks cannot touch.
    *   **Sashigane:** Divide grid into L shaped blocks (one block wide), cells with open circles form the knee (bend), number in open circle shows cells in block, arrows form one end.
    *   **Shikaku:** Divide grid into rectangles with numbers, each rectangle contains only one number showing its cell count.

**IV. Number Placement/Filling**

*   **A. Filling Cells with Numbers:**
    *   **Choco Banana:** Fill empty cells with numbers, each block contains one number or "?", blocks form a chain, chain cannot contain more than one block of one size/shape.
    *   **Hebi:** Place numbers 1-5 sequentially connected in white squares (snakes), snakes cannot touch, black squares show nearest snake number in arrow direction.
    *   **Nansuke:** Fill blank cells with numbers from a list, numbers are up-down or left to right, one cell has only one number.
    *   **Ripple Effect:** Fill empty cells with numbers, each room contains consecutive numbers starting from 1, if number duplicated in row/column, space between must be equal to or larger than value.
    *   **Sudoku:** Place numbers 1-9 in empty cells, each row, column, and 3x3 block contains all numbers 1-9.

**V. Movement Puzzles**

*   **A. Moving Elements:**
    *   **Satogaeri:** Move circles (vertically or horizontally) so each "country" contains one circle, numbers indicate cells to pass through, circles cannot cross tracks or go over other circles.
    *   **Yosenabe:** Move all circles (vertically or horizontally) into gray areas, show movement by arrow, number in gray area equals total of numbers of circles entering it.
